english.title: Attempt to pay for the sexual services of a boy 13 to 15 - no penetration - SOA 2003

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) An act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which, constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 01/09/1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he/she may have proceedings brought against them in the United Kingdom (section 72).
(ii) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act where payment is for sexual services of a child - if the victim or (as the case may be) other party was under 16, and the offender was 18 or over, or is or has been sentenced in respect of the offence to imprisonment for a term of at least 12 months. (Sch 3 paragraph 29).

other.penalty: Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates' court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020. On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited. Time limit for prosecutions:None
